settings.name_in_paper: n-armed dueling bandits, Borda winner identification
settings.definition_quote: we choose a pair of arms $(i,j)$ to duel, and receive one bit indicating which of the two is better or preferred, with the probability of $i$ winning the duel is equal to a constant $p_{i,j}$ ... The \textit{Borda} winner is an arm $b$ that satisfies $\sum_{j\neq b} p_{b,j} \geq \sum_{j\neq i} p_{i,j}$ ... We assume throughout this paper that there exists a unique Borda winner.

conditions: any delta-PAC dueling bandits algorithm for the Borda winner

source.quote: Consider a matrix $P$ such that $\frac{3}{8} \leq p_{i,j} \leq \frac{5}{8}, \forall i,j \in [n]$ with $n \geq 4$. Let $\tau$ be the total number of duels. Then for $\delta \leq 0.15$, any $\delta$-PAC dueling bandits algorithm to find the Borda winner has $$\E_P[\tau] \geq C \log \frac{1}{2\delta} \sum\limits_{i \neq 1}^{} \frac{1}{(s_1-s_i)^2} $$ ... Furthermore, $C$ can be chosen to be $1/90$.

results.notes: Delta_i denotes the Borda gap s_1 - s_i (Borda score = mean of the Borda-reduced bandit). n = K arms.

conditions: any delta-PAC dueling bandits algorithm for the Borda winner

source.quote: Consider a matrix $P$ such that $\frac{3}{8} \leq p_{i,j} \leq \frac{5}{8}, \forall i,j \in [n]$, and $n \geq 3$. Then for $\delta \leq 0.15$, any $\delta$-PAC dueling bandits algorithm to find the Borda winner has $$\E_P[\tau] \geq C \left( \frac{n-2}{n-1} \right)^2 \left( \sum\limits_{i \neq 1}^{} \frac{1}{(s_1-s_i)^2} \right) \log \frac{1}{2\delta}$$ ... $C$ can be chosen to be $\tfrac{1}{40}$.

results.notes: Appendix restatement of Theorem 1 with explicit (n-2)/(n-1) factor; Delta_i = s_1 - s_i.

symbols.R: solution of (32/R^2) log(32 n/(delta R^2)) = T_0
symbols.k_sp: sparsity level k input to the algorithm

conditions: for every i != 1, either {p_{1,w}-p_{i,w}} is (1/3,k)-approximately sparse or s_1 - s_i >= R

source.label: sparseTheorem
source.quote: Let $k \geq 0$ and $T_0>0$ be inputs to the above algorithm and let $R$ be the solution to $\frac{32 }{R^2} \log\left( \frac{32 n/ \delta}{R^2 } \right) = T_0$. If for all $i \in [n] \setminus 1$, at least one of the following holds: 1. ... is $(\tfrac{1}{3},k)$-approximately sparse, 2. $(s_1-s_i) \geq R$, then with probability at least $1- 3\delta$, the algorithm returns the best arm after no more than ... samples where $\Delta_{j}:= s_{1} - s_j$ and $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-3delta (correctness and sample bound). Delta_i = Borda gap s_1 - s_i. Unspecified absolute constant c -> O notation.
